newsitem.title: CHINA: Rains help ease drought in four Chinese provinces.
newsitem.headline: Rains help ease drought in four Chinese provinces.

text.p: Rains have helped ease a drought in four Chinese provinces, officials said on Wednesday.

Rainfall has reduced the acreage of crops affected by the drought in eastern Shandong province to 1.8 million hectares from 3.33 million hectares in early July, an official of the provincial agricultural department said.

Shandong recorded 77 millimetres of rain between June and mid-July, down 62 percent from a year ago, but it helped to reduce the drought in the province, the official said. He declined to give further details.

In northern Shanxi and northeastern Heilongjiang, heavy rainfall between July 17 and 20 had eased the drought in most parts of the two provinces, officials of the provincial drought relief offices said.
In northern Hebei province near Beijing, drizzles over the past four days have helped ease the drought, a provincial agricultural official said.
The officials declined to give further details.
While drought and high temperatures have been plaguing northern China, floods have wreaked havoc in the south.
